Charred remains of the note serve as your only guide.

<The faint radiance of the embers darkening, you stumble across the remnants of a recent fire.

Amidst the scattered provisions, you discover a blistered note.>

"Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place."
As you stumble upon the remnants of yet another charred corpse, your gaze falls upon a message secured to a wooden plank.
Repelling Invaders
Bring the Warsong Outrider Mark to Felore Moonray, Priestess of the Moon, at the Moonwell base in Ashenvale.
Some of the Warsong Outriders lie defeated, but the battle still rages...
Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography
Have you brought something to add to our collection?

Thank you, $N. You say this is from the Ironforge library? ...I'm sure they won't miss it.

If you discover more magical works that might benefit the library, please bring them to me.

Clear the Forest!
Bring the Silverwing Sentinel Charm to Kazragore, Far Seer, at the Bonfire base in Ashenvale.
This one is slain, but these infuriating alliance continue to fight... what is this charm?
Stepping Stones
You tear the note from the plank and read the scrawled writing.

The note begins, "Mission said they were both making deliveries for New Plague. Looks like simple apothecary accidents to me. Find my cozy spot in the mountains between The Barrens and Desolace if you want a safe place to talk."
Backcountry adventurers and mercenaries alike undoubtedly make camp here. The corner of a note flapping in the breeze catches your eye and you reach for it.
Highway Robbery
Find someone in Desolace who knows about the pillaged campsite.

The campsite before you is a grisly scene. Judging by the remains, the victims were two humans and a dwarf. Markings on the bones indicate a savage attack, but the looted supplies tell you this wasn't done by an animal. The wounds don't match centaur weaponry either.

Perhaps an experienced scavenger of these lands would know what to make of this.
On the Lam
Find one of the Desolace marauders.

I've found a couple of scenes like you describe, $n. Always camps of humans and dwarves. Rumor among the caravans is a group of Horde marauders did it. Seems likely given the victims, and how brutal the attacks were.

Apparently the bandits fled Desolace once an Alliance marshal got hot on their trail.

If you're looking to track one of 'em down, I'd check Booty Bay. Ports always have shady characters coming and going. You might catch one trying to get a boat to somewhere.
Cherry for Your Thoughts?
Bring a Cherry Grog to Tokal, in Booty Bay, to hear the rest of her story.

You with the marshal? No, you don't look like it.

The rumors you've heard are only half true. Yes, we were pillaging human and dwarven camps, but we weren't doing it for the Horde. We were privately employed.

I'll tell you the whole story if you buy me some grog.
No Honor Among Thieves
Find Illari Duskfeather on the coast of Arathi Highlands, and get access to her cache of stolen loot.

As I was saying...

Our boss wasn't with the Horde. She was a night elf named Illari Duskfeather. She gave us intel on the camps, and even let us keep most of the loot. She only kept a few of the rarer finds.

Once the marshal was on our tail, though, she left us for dead. I don't know her motives, but I think we were set up as patsies.

I'm not the vengeful type, but I won't stop someone else from hunting her down. If you're looking for her, she once mentioned a hideout on the coast of Arathi.
Storm, Earth, and Fire
Collect $1oa Twisted Fire Totems, $2oa Twisted Earth Totems, $3oa Twisted Air Totems, and $4oa Twisted Water Totems for Veyric Thunderhame in Arathi Highlands.

Floodin' the Thousand Needles is no small feat, $n. If I hadn't felt the elements' outrage meself, I'd have never believed it. But here we are.

The quilboar aren't the first tae weaponize the elements irresponsibly, and they won't be the last. If we want to prepare our own counter-ritual, we'll need a better understanding of these twisted elements. Take this book. It details the many denizens of Azeroth and how they practice shamanism.

If you can learn from them, maybe we can find a solution.
Elemental Aid
Defeat Charlga Razorflank in Razorfen Kraul and collect information on the quilboar's plans.

Now that you have mastered the elements, you have an obligation to them, and thus to all of Azeroth herself. We call to them for aid, we do not demand their power. It is time you return the favors granted to you. And I think I know how.

The quilboar twist the elements for their own ends, and seem to be extending their reach within these borders. Go into their kraul and put an end to whatever they scheme. These lands must be protected.
Storm, Earth, and Fire
Collect $1oa Twisted Fire Totems, $2oa Twisted Earth Totems, $3oa Twisted Air Totems, and $4oa Twisted Water Totems for Prate Cloudseer in Thousand Needles.

So the quilboar mean to flood the Thousand Needles with their twisted shamanism, do they? It seems almost unimaginable, but you yourself have seen that these creatures are not to be taken lightly.

I had wished to continue your training in earnest, but there is no time for that now. These lands are home to many different creatures, friend and foe alike, and none of them deserve such a fate. We must act.

Take this tome. It was meant for study, but may now hold the key to dispersing this coming storm.
Grant's Shield
Find Grant's Mace on one of the skeletons in Raven Hill Cemetery then return to Sirra Von'Indie in Darkshire for more information.

A shield left behind by the specter of Grant Valor, father of the Valor family and hero of Raven Hill.

With Grant's spirit still battling the undead, perhaps his unfinished business was to slay the scourge that injured him in the Raven Hill Cemetery. It is likely the one his mace is still imbedded in.
Silvia's Sword
Defeat $1oa Defias Night Blades and $1oa Defias Enchanters in Addle's Stead then return to Sirra Von'Indi in Darkshire for more information.

A sword left by the spirit of Raven Hill's guard, Silvia Valor, who lived her life protecting civilians and their homes.

With Silvia's spirit still visiting farmsteads, perhaps her unfinished business was to route the defias who have taken up residence in Addle's Stead south of Raven Hill.
Eyes on the Sky
Speak with Prate Cloudseer in Thousand Needles.

The note you found says the Razormane have burrowed into the Thousand Needles for some sort of unseen ritual. Raging storms and rising tides...

The quilboar must be using some cruel sorcery they learned from Hirzek, a shaman who went to great lengths to twist the elements. If they plan to flood the canyon, this would require devastating elemental powers.

We are ill equipped to deal with this, but a powerful shaman like you must have an idea. Return to your allies and see if you can't find an answer.
With Wind Beneath Your Wings
Return to Rau Cliffrunner in Thousand Needles at Freewind Post.

Here mon, a Squall-breakers Potion be what you need. Drink this to protect yourself against the elements of the storm, but remember it only goin' to last for a short while.$B$BNow go, return to your friends in need. There's nothing more I can do for you.
Heed My Call
Use the Twisted Totems to put an end to the quilboar ritual.

Now that you have the twisted totems, we must wield them to summon forth the corrupted elementals the quilboar are calling upon. Defeat them to cleanse these lands and put an end to the Razormane's abominable ritual then report back to Rau Cliffrunner with your success.

You should begin your clensing at the steam pools to the west. That area is rich with each of the elements. But be careful, $n. The quilboar will not sit idly while you interrupt their plans.
The Tempest's Weapons
Deliver the Eye of the Tempest to Bath'rah the Windwatcher in Alterac Mountains.

Our people cannot thank you enough, but I have no real use for this eye. I have heard of an old shaman in the Alterac mountains that has an eye for storm elemental magic. Perhaps he may be able to craft something for you.
Basilisks: Should Petrification be Feared?
Greater Friend of the Library
Anyone Can Cook
Find an ogre who can read the Illegible Recipe.

The recipe appears to be for some sort of meat dish. It is written in a language you don't understand. Ogre is your best guess, given the source and subject matter.

Ogres aren't usually culinary types but, if you knew one with such an inclination, they could translate the recipe for you.
A Ticking Present
The Troll Scroll
Solve the riddle of the scroll. Once you've done that, Hemet Nesingwary might like to hear the tale.

<The ancient glyphs resolve into words before your eyes.>

When Zul'Kunda's fountain runs with the waters of the holy spring, the gods grant their blessing.
Geomancy: The Stone-Cold Truth
Defensive Magics 101
A Web of Lies: Debunking Myths and Legends
Demons and You
Mummies: A Guide to the Unsavory Undead
RwlRwlRwlRwl!
Wet Job
Dusting off a messenger bag emerging from the soil, you find a parchment nestled among the supplies.

"Always like to keep a reserve stash nearby in the off chance I've got to flee in a hurry.

The face of this mountainside is so beautiful you might say it was carved from the waterfalls of time. 
That's the eagles nest, that's what you're looking for."
Dwarven Engineering, always a marvel.
Eagle's Fist
Water spray dampens the air, the view is incredible.

<You find a carefully folded letter inside of the toolbox.>

"From here, with the right tools, you call the shots. Great place to launch a parachute glider.

My loyalty to the Eagle and Fist requires distance in order to serve them best. This barricade has had better days, like the Old Kingdoms it once defended, but I'll never abandon it."
A campfire is newly fed with wood, but signs of a quick departure are evident.
This Must Be The Place
Whoever was here, you just missed them.

"So, I've decided to take my work back underground. To stop it falling into the wrong hands."

<The paper is torn just large enough to fit the message. You aren't sure if these are the last words you'll read from the author, or if they're a clue to the next hideout. An inadequately secured sleeping bag is unrolling itself onto your feet...>
Heavy canvas is rolled over assorted equipment. You help yourself to the pack.
Scramble
Find what awaits you.

"Not so bad, eh? Since you're reading this, it means my stash is still there. Take a hundred paces due north and don't break your ankles going down the steep cliffside. There should be enough to keep you going."
You pull a messenger bag out of the ground. Stuffed in with the supplies is a dirty parchment.
